decision_note: Banksia reproductive-biology/mating-system study concerns pollination and breeding biology without a focal plant antagonist/exploiter response.
Kigelia reproductive-biology study addresses pollination/reproduction without a focal plant antagonist/exploiter response.
Alfalfa reproductive-ecology review is centered on pollination and seed production rather than a measured plant mutualist-antagonist floral coordinate.
Agastache reproductive-ecology study for pollinator gardens focuses pollination service without a focal plant antagonist/exploiter channel.
Western silvery aster reproductive-ecology study lacks a focal measured plant antagonist/exploiter response.
Annual-plant reproductive-escape study measures response to butterfly eggs/herbivory and accelerated seed production without a focal pollinator service/response.
Roscoea reproductive-isolation study concerns pollination and species integrity without a focal plant antagonist/exploiter response.
Restoration-oriented reproductive-phenology study lacks a focal floral trait/reward coordinate with pollinator and antagonist responses.
Midge-orchid study measures fly pollination and reproductive success without a focal plant antagonist/exploiter response.
Cabralea reproductive-success study in forest fragments does not establish a focal pollinator-antagonist floral coordinate.
Florivory study measures resilience of floral scent emission after damage but does not directly measure pollinator response/service in the focal experiment.
Primary Caladenia tessellata study jointly evaluates post-fire pollination success, herbivory and mycorrhizal context; retain for multi-agent reproductive-context adjudication.
Oak acorn-allocation study concerns resource allocation to seed production and water-use strategy rather than a focal floral coordinate and pollinator response.
Resource-heterogeneity/biodiversity-function study is not a focal floral trait or plant pollinator-antagonist system.
Review of homoterpenes concerns arthropod-plant chemical ecology broadly, primarily herbivore/enemy signalling rather than a focal measured pollinator channel on a floral coordinate.
Primary ant-plant-pollinator study explicitly tests how defensive-ant identity affects pollination and plant fitness; retain for mutualist-identity and pollination-cost adjudication.
Ceropegia pollination study identifies key fly pollinators of foetid-scented flowers but lacks a focal plant antagonist/exploiter response.
Arabidopsis aromatic-aldehyde-synthase study connects wounding/herbivory response and flower scent biosynthesis but does not measure pollinator ecological response to the scent phenotype.
Bumblebee avoidance of contaminated flowers concerns pollinator behavioural immunity/contamination rather than a focal plant antagonist/exploiter response.

Primary Cucumis study manipulates root herbivory, measures pollinator visitation, pollen receipt and fruit production, and recovers indirect and direct fitness effects; retain for herbivory-pollination-performance adjudication.
General review of plant volatile chemistry/biosynthesis and environmental interactions is too broad to serve as an independent primary study or focused SCH synthesis.

Primary passion-flower study directly evaluates ant defence and pollination, testing whether protective ants interfere with floral visitors; retain for defence-pollination functional-boundary adjudication.
New Phytologist commentary 'Safe sex in plants' is not an independent primary study or substantive focused synthesis for the systematic evidence count.

Swedish-language summary/identity of the Arabidopsis lyrata plant-animal interaction programme covers pollinator- and herbivore-mediated selection on flowering and floral display; retain and resolve programme/report dependence with SCHPRISMA-000664 at full text.
Primary hawthorn fragmentation study jointly measures pollination, frugivory and seed predation across spatial scales; retain for multi-function landscape-context adjudication.
